name: When should I repair rotten siding versus replacing an entire section or wall?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair rotten siding versus replacing an entire section or wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision to repair or replace depends on the extent of the rot and the overall condition of the surrounding siding. If the rot is localized to a few boards and hasn't compromised the structural integrity of the wall, a targeted repair is often sufficient. However, if the rot is widespread, affects multiple layers, or has penetrated the sheathing underneath, replacing a larger section or even an entire wall of siding might be a more cost-effective and durable solution in the long run. We assess the damage thoroughly to recommend the most appropriate and lasting approach for your home.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair localized rot if limited to a few boards; replace larger sections or walls if rot is widespread or affects structural integrity. Assessment helps determine the best approach.
